items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: Five saxes. Jack Cordero tenor; George Bandford from Boston, flute and tenor; Charlie Strickfaden oboe and baritone; Frankie Trumbauer and I sat next, together

ctx.x: How much did it cost for a room for a week in New York at that time.

Oh well with the Whiteman band hotel rooms were so reasonable. We used to get a rate. $2.50 single. Not the Waldorf, but good hotels. No flea bags. Like Goldie used to say, no flea bags you know. And it was great traveling with the band, the Whiteman band. And I’ll never forget. See I joined spring of ’36. But I was doing the radio show. Woodbury Hollow Soap Hour. And I just did that. The rest of the band, they were doing Jumbo. Billy Rose’s Jumbo at the Hippodrome Theater, it was on Sixth Avenue just north of…
What was he like? Was he friendly? Easy to get along with?
